To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
information behavior and information practice are both useful umbrella concepts for information seeking studies.
information behavior and information practice are umbrella concepts denoting general ways in which humans deal with information.
the discourses on information behavior and information practice are quite fragmented, and the two discourses are not in any way mutually exclusive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discursive nature and the epistemological and ontological assumptions underlying the two major umbrella concepts of information seeking studies, information behavior and information practice.
a critical analysis of information behavior and information practice as umbrella concepts, with the purpose to contribute to the self reflection of information seeking studies.
the discourses on information behavior and information practice and their relation to each other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
information seeking studies are currently dominated by the discourse on information behavior and that information practice is not yet sufficiently elaborated to be a viable alternative.
information behavior and information practice have different discursive origins and different implications.
information practice is a critical alternative to information behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have to take into account that the information behavior concept is not only a concept of information seeking studies but a part of the broader discourse of information behavior.
we are in need of a new, more encompassing, and less fragmentary discourse, in order to make sense of the information seeking phenomena in a broader sense.
we need a more critical approach to the discursive formations of information seeking studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

information seeking studies should be more critical of the discourses that inform them, and that researchers should be more self reflective of the ways in which their research is informed by the discursive formations they are part of.
researchers should be aware of the fact that the discourses of information behavior and information practice are not only different but also have their limitations.
the two discourses are not as different as it may seem at first glance.
